newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey sees 1996 trade deficit at $19-20 billion.
newsitem.headline: Turkey sees 1996 trade deficit at $19-20 billion.

text.p: Turkey's trade deficit in 1996 is expected to be $19-$20 billion, based on mid-December data, State Minister Ayfer Yilmaz said.
"When we look at provisional figures by December 15, it is expected that exports will be around $22 billion-$23 billion and imports at $42 billion," Yilmaz told journalists.
Imports were previously forecast to be around $40 billion and exports at $22 billion. Yilmaz, who is in charge of foreign trade, said final 1996 trade figures would be published on February 15.
Speaking to journalists on Thursday evening, Yilmaz said there was concern that in 1997, as in 1996, exporters would be unable to meet their targets.
Turkey's 1997 official foreign trade targets are $29 billion of exports and $50 billion of imports.
Yilmaz forecast in October a 1996 deficit of $20 billion, compared with an earlier government target of $16 billion and a 1995 deficit of $14.1 billion.

In 1996 falls in exports in the key sectors of textiles and clothing played a notable role in the larger-than-expected trade deficit. Clothing exports shrank eight percent year-on-year because of stagnation in European markets, she said.
On the import side, an expected rise in consumer goods imports failed to materialise while investment goods imports were in line with expectations.
